text:
Ivy: quick ping  after the launch post went live we saw an odd shift in the weekly KPI view: demo-requests ticked down 11% but webinar regs up 9%. dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/r/kpis/launch-0310 :eyes:

Omar: saw the same. suspicious that inbound lead routing rules flipped for the new launch CTA. some leads are being classified as 'nurture' instead of 'sales' which changes downstream MQL counts.

Sophie: ran a small check comparing form_variant -> lead_route

```
SELECT form_variant, lead_route, count(*) AS n
FROM events.webinar_reg
WHERE day='2026-03-10'
GROUP BY 1,2
ORDER BY n DESC
LIMIT 20;
```

Grant: i deployed a messaging tweak in the header CTA yesterday (shorter copy + hidden field 'intent_level=low'). that could be changing the routing logic that looks for 'high_intent' hidden field.

Maya: ok let's separate concerns: 1) attribution/dashboard: are we sure it's routing vs attribution? 2) messaging: did the copy or hidden fields change routing rules? 3) KPI report: we should add a footnote in Friday's weekly KPI review.

KPI-Bot: alert: demo_request_rate_drop anomaly (z=3.6) at 2026-03-10 14:07 UTC for NA cohort.

Ivy: Omar can you diff the closed-loop match (sales-accepted leads) vs dashboard counts for last 48h? include routing field.

Omar: on it. initial diff shows ~210 leads were routed to 'nurture' that the old logic would have sent to 'sales'. that's ~10% of expected demo pipeline.

Sophie: looks like form_variant 'B' included the hidden field change. old parsing rule only looked for 'high_intent' or 'hi_intent'. since 'intent_level=low' is present we hit fallback.

Grant: my fault on the hidden field rename, apologies. quick fix: i'll revert to the original hidden field name and push a small copy update that keeps tracking stable. ETA 20m.

Maya: actionables: @Grant revert hidden field + copy; @Omar re-run routing simulation and post corrected counts; @Sophie mark affected rows in /shared/marketing/launch-issues/3141592653.csv so we can reassign for KPI snapshot. We'll include a short note in the weekly KPI review about the messaging-induced routing change. Can we get an updated KPI snapshot before EOD?

Omar: running simulation now. if we reassign the 210 leads back to 'sales' demo-request rate recovers ~9% and projected demo pipeline recovers ~12% in the weekly view.

Grant: reverted and redeployed. monitoring incoming signups and routing. adding a QA test to the launch checklist so hidden field names are preserved.

Sophie: flagged affected rows and uploaded CSV to /shared/marketing/launch-issues/3141592653.csv with sample ids and timestamps.

KPI-Bot: note added to weekly_kpi_review (2026-03-12): messaging hidden-field rename impacted lead routing and demo counts. reference: https://dash.redwood.ai/r/notes/3141592653-note

Ivy: thanks. couple meta-suggestions for the weekly notes: 1) call out 'routing vs attribution' distinction with small examples, 2) recommend a post-launch QA checklist item to validate hidden fields and routing rules, 3) suggest a small dashboard column showing 'routing_confidence' so quick eyeballing avoids misinterpretation.

Maya: agreed on all. @Omar can you add the before/after snapshot link to the Friday deck? @Grant make a ticket for the QA checklist addition.

Omar: posted updated snapshot: https://dash.redwood.ai/r/perf/launch-reassigned (includes corrected demo-request rate).

Grant: ticket created: MKT-4876 (add launch hidden-field QA).

Maya: wrapping up  we'll mention this in the KPI review as an execution note rather than a product change. thanks everyone. closing thread. :lock:
